A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DiScoFormer and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The retained material can be matched across renumbering and relocation, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original density and score estimation experiments, non-Gaussian generalization tests, Landau simulations, attention analyses, and runtime measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds a 100-dimensional estimation experiment and a controlled whitening ablation in Tables 4 and 5.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the training objective explicitly change the density target from f to log f; Figure 2 correspondingly replaces determinant multiplication with an additive log-determinant correction. This revises the stated training and output specification while retaining the joint Transformer architecture. Because v2 already discusses log-density variants, this does not establish a newly implemented model. The squared-norm lift belongs to the new theoretical construction.

E1.justification: v3 substantially extends the tested input regimes with 100-dimensional, two-component GMM estimation and a new scale-extrapolation scenario using log-uniform distributions over GMM locations and scales. Earlier experiments reached dimension 10 and tested additional modes and non-Gaussian distributions. Those experiments and the downstream applications remain.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds an Oracle h KDE comparator whose fixed bandwidth is selected by grid search. Existing KDE, SD-KDE, and sliced-score-matching comparisons remain. The widespread Silverman-to-Scott relabeling does not establish a comparator replacement: the displayed bandwidth formula and retained plot results are unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include a six-layer, width-256 model evaluated after 150,000 training steps with 2,048 context points and 256 queries, plus matched whitening/no-whitening models under ID and OOD conditions. The reported default GMM covariance range changes from [0,1]^d to [0.2,1]^d, and the entropy estimator's missing minus sign is corrected. These specification changes do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Table 5 introduce a controlled investigation of the central whitening component, measuring its contribution to score and log-density estimation under ordinary and extreme-scale conditions. v2 measured overall equivariance but did not isolate whitening. Existing attention, test-time-training, mode-generalization, and score-matching analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains averaging over 50 trials. Neither version adds seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for the benchmark results. The new tables follow the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: New results establish performance in two additional regimes. Table 4 reports score/log-density MSE of 0.167/20.8 for DiScoFormer versus 1.090/781 for Oracle h KDE. Table 5 reports OOD score MSE of 0.020 with whitening versus 1.136 without it. Tables 1–3 and matched earlier plots retain their numerical findings; the additions are not same-setting improvements over v2.

T1.justification: The constant-norm self-attention identity is extended to arbitrary-input cross-attention and constructive exact KDE score/log-density recovery, with explicit lifting and normalizer requirements and supporting counterexamples. Appendix B adds an adaptive-bandwidth proposition and a generalization theorem under boundedness, stability, and GMM-risk assumptions. Proposition 3.1 and its proof also correct the score transformation to P S(X) A^(-T).

C1.justification: The central reusable-estimator, accuracy, and downstream-application claims remain. The theoretical contribution is broadened and made more specific: the conclusion now claims exact KDE-score representation on squared-norm-lifted inputs, whereas v2 emphasized recovery of normalized KDE weights. The added experiments support existing scalability claims rather than introducing a different research objective.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive applicability limits: distributions far from the GMM training family may require adaptation, and asymptotic consistency remains unproved. It explains the conditional nature of the generalization theorem, interprets whitening as adaptive bandwidth selection, and attributes scale robustness to whitening using the new ablation. Approximate rotation equivariance was already acknowledged in v2.

D1.justification: Figure 2 explains the matrix inverse square root and output coordinate corrections. Section 4.1 specifies query-only differentiation for test-time training, with context held fixed using stopgrad. Table 4 supplies architecture, training-step, context-size, and query-size details for the added experiment. Most standard architecture and hardware information is retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Ilin and Hu's 2026 Vlasov–Maxwell–Landau paper and removes Ilin's 2025 Landau relative-entropy stability paper. Attention positioning now emphasizes arbitrary-query cross-attention beyond constant-norm formulations. The publication update for Score-based deterministic density sampling refers to the same work and is not an additional citation.

P1.justification: The downstream sections on relative Fisher information, density estimation, entropy/Fisher information, and plasma simulation are substantially rewritten and compressed, including removal of a duplicated comparator list. Empirical attention verification becomes a separate subsection, and the appendix hierarchy is reorganized. The abstract, conclusion, author affiliations, and publication front matter are also revised.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 4–5, expands Figure 2 and its caption, exchanges the numbering of Figures 4 and 5, and consolidates retained Figures 7–11 onto page 9. Appendix figures are repositioned alongside their discussions. Most underlying graphics remain unchanged; KDE captions now say Scott, although Figure 7 retains its internal Silverman label.

improvement.justification: The clearer log-density specification, corrected score-transformation and entropy formulas, explicit KDE constructions, and new high-dimensional and whitening tests improve clarity and support relative to v2. The added limitations also better qualify generalization claims. These gains are tempered by a new mathematical overstatement: Appendix B.2's claimed O(K^(-2s/d)) density rate does not follow from a bound retaining an O(K^(-s/d)) total-variation term. The net improvement is positive but limited.
